meta.scenario: T2 enters as a looped phrase — fade-in loop strategy

transition_arc: T1 is in its main groove, T2 has a strong clean 4-bar loop candidate at bar 8. Instead of a straight fade_in, T2 enters as a looped phrase — the same 4-bar groove repeating 3 times (12 bars). During those 12 bars, T2 fades up from near-silence to audible presence. The loop break (play(T2) at fade_in end) is the 'moment' — T2 snaps out of the loop and plays freely, which creates a natural tension-and-release that the straight fade_in lacks. 11A to 10A is a -1 Camelot move, fully compatible.

annotated_actions.why: Kill T2 bass before fade starts. T2 will loop while fading in — no bass yet.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 8 (from_bar for fade_in): clean 4-bar groove, drums=0.9, harmonic=0.7, vocals=0.00. This section repeats well — identical to the next 4 bars.
annotated_actions.why: T2 enters as a looped phrase. loop(T2) locks T2's audio to a 4-bar phrase repeating 3 times (12 bars). Combined with fade_in, T2 fades up while stuck on this groove. The listener hears T2 as a rising rhythmic texture, not a new track yet. The loop break at bar 76 is the 'moment' — T2 suddenly plays freely, a natural tension release.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 from_bar=8: kick present, bass=0.0 (eq), groove locked at bar 8 by loop
annotated_actions.why: Fade_in + loop together: T2 fades from 0 to 1.0 over 12 bars while the loop holds it at the 4-bar phrase. The gain ramp is continuous; the loop just holds the audio source position. from_bar=8 is where the loop candidate starts in T2's audio.
T1 and T2 will blend for 12 bars. T1 harmonic content is active — cutting T1 mids to 0.45 prevents harmonic pile-up as T2 rises. T1 is fading out, so no restore needed.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 72: 8 bars into fade window, T1 groove still active
annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 16 in source (= 8 + 8 elapsed via loop): fade_in at 67% complete
annotated_actions.why: Midpoint of the 12-bar blend. T2 is prominent enough to take the bass. Swap at bar 72 (= 64 + 8) — roughly 67% through.
Restore T2 bass at swap point. T2 bass arrives as T1 bass cuts.

annotated_actions.t1_state: T1 bar 64: start fade simultaneously with T2 fade_in
annotated_actions.why: T1 fades out over the same 12-bar window T2 fades in. Equal-power crossfade feel.

annotated_actions.t2_state: T2 bar 20 (= from_bar 8 + duration_bars 12): T2 full groove, post-loop
annotated_actions.why: play(T2) fires at fade_in end (64 + 12 = 76). This BREAKS THE LOOP — T2 resumes from bar 20 (where it would be without the loop). The loop break creates a 'snap' moment: T2 was repeating the same 4 bars, then suddenly progresses. This is the energy release that makes the loop-fade technique more dynamic than a straight blend. from_bar=20 = fade_in.from_bar (8) + fade_in.duration_bars (12).
